{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Patch testing requires 3 additional visits during screening, increasing burden",
      "quote": "Patients will be called to the site for 3 visits for the patch testing",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The patch testing procedure requires three separate visits (application, day 2 reading, day 3-7 reading) in addition to the screening visit, significantly increasing patient burden and site workload during the screening period.",
      "fix": "Consider consolidating patch test readings or allowing remote/self-reading where feasible, or reduce the number of required visits by combining with other scheduled visits if possible."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing washout periods may delay screening and cause scheduling issues",
      "quote": "4 weeks for other systemic immunomodulators such as cyclosporine (CsA), mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), methotrexate (MTX), Alitretinoin, systemic JAK inhibitors etc.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The 4-week washout for systemic immunomodulators may extend the screening period, potentially causing patients to miss the Day -56 to Day -1 window and increasing screen failure rates.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing a longer screening window or providing guidance on how to handle patients who require longer washout periods."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing results may be outdated if not repeated within 3 years",
      "quote": "In case of patients who have had patch testing with the same country-specific series of allergens within 3 years prior to screening visit, the patch testing does not need to be repeated",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 3-year validity of previous patch test results may be inconsistent with the need for current eligibility determination, as allergen sensitivities can change over time.",
      "fix": "Clarify the rationale for the 3-year window and ensure it aligns with standard practice or update to a shorter timeframe."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing readings may require additional unscheduled visits beyond day 7",
      "quote": "In some patients a reading after day 7 may be taken when the clinical history strongly supports sensitization.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The possibility of a reading after day 7 may necessitate additional unscheduled visits, increasing patient burden and site coordination complexity.",
      "fix": "Plan for potential extended readings in the schedule and communicate this to sites to manage patient expectations."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing application site may be unsuitable, requiring alternative sites",
      "quote": "The upper back is preferred site for the application of patch tests. In case not suitable for patch testing, or is fully used already, the upper parts of the arm may be used.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Using the upper arm as an alternative may affect patch test accuracy and interpretation, but this is a standard fallback.",
      "fix": "Provide clear guidance on how to document and interpret results when alternative sites are used."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing requires discontinuation of therapies, which may impact patient safety",
      "quote": "Patients need to discontinue therapies for AD before the patch testing is conducted.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Discontinuing AD therapies for up to 4 weeks may lead to disease flares and increased patient discomfort, potentially affecting compliance and safety.",
      "fix": "Consider providing rescue therapy guidance or a tapering plan to minimize flares during the washout period."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing adds significant time to the screening visit",
      "quote": "Patch testing with a standard series of allergens will be conducted during the screening period for determining eligibility.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The patch testing procedure itself is time-consuming and may prolong the screening visit, which already includes many other assessments.",
      "fix": "Consider scheduling patch testing on a separate day from other screening procedures to reduce visit duration."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patch testing results may be affected by concurrent skin conditions",
      "quote": "The patch test should be applied on normal appearing skin free from skin diseases such as AD.",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Patients with widespread AD may lack suitable normal skin for patch testing, potentially leading to delays or inability to perform the test.",
      "fix": "Provide guidance on how to handle patients with extensive skin involvement, such as using alternative sites or postponing testing until skin clears."
    }
  ]
}
